_note: Indian Railways luggage rules (baggage/train-luggage-rules.html). Checked against indianrail.gov.in 'Rules for luggage' and parcel.indianrail.gov.in on 26 Nov 2026 (first checked 3 Nov 2026). Re-check every 3 months. Items from news only are labelled as such in the text.
quick: Free luggage: 70 kg in AC First, 50 kg in AC 2-tier and First Class, 40 kg in AC 3-tier, AC Chair Car and Sleeper, and 35 kg in Second Class.
You can carry more in your coach if you book it at the luggage office and pay 1.5 times the luggage rate: up to 150 kg in AC First, 100 kg in AC 2-tier, 80 kg in Sleeper and 70 kg in Second Class.
In AC 3-tier and AC Chair Car, 40 kg is also the maximum. Anything more must go in the luggage van.
Suitcases up to 100 x 60 x 25 cm can go in the compartment. In AC 3-tier and AC Chair Car the limit is smaller: 55 x 45 x 22.5 cm.
Children aged 5 to 11 get half the adult allowance, up to 50 kg.
Book extra weight at the station's luggage office before you travel and you pay 1.5 times the luggage rate. If staff find unbooked extra luggage on the train, you pay six times the rate.
allowance_note: The maximum includes the free allowance. Book anything above the free allowance at the station's luggage office before you travel. Indian Railways also allows a small margin (15 kg in AC First, 10 kg in other classes) before the heaviest penalty applies, but that extra weight is still charged.

size.text: Trunks, suitcases and boxes up to 100 x 60 x 25 cm (length x breadth x height, measured outside) can be carried in the compartment as personal luggage. In AC 3-tier and AC Chair Car coaches the maximum is 55 x 45 x 22.5 cm, about the size of a small cabin trolley. Bigger luggage must travel in the brake van (luggage van), and an oversized trunk found in the compartment is charged and moved there.

excess: Booked extra luggage that travels with you in the coach costs 1.5 times the luggage rate, with a minimum charge of ₹30. If staff find unbooked luggage over your allowance during the journey or at your destination, the extra weight is charged at six times the luggage rate, with a minimum of ₹50. If it is over the free allowance but within the small margin, it is charged at 1.5 times the rate instead.
rate_note: There is no single price per kg. The luggage rate (Scale L) depends on the weight and the distance, and Indian Railways says it is 80% higher than its standard parcel rate (Scale P). The station's luggage office tells you the exact charge, and the Indian Railways parcel website has a freight calculator for an estimate.
booking_steps: Pack the luggage securely and label it with your name and address in English or Hindi. Luggage without a clear address isn't accepted.
Go to the luggage office (parcel office) at your boarding station with your journey ticket, at least 30 minutes before the train's departure time.
Pay the charge. You get a luggage ticket, and staff note it on your journey ticket.
At your destination, show the ticket and the luggage ticket to collect anything that travelled in the luggage van.
booking: If you book your seat in advance, you can book your luggage in advance at the same time. Extra weight within your class's maximum can travel with you in the coach. Anything above that, and trunks or suitcases bigger than the size limit, travel in the brake van (luggage van) of your train. In AC 3-tier and AC Chair Car, 40 kg is the most you can keep in the coach, so all extra weight goes in the luggage van.
not_allowed: Explosive, dangerous or inflammable things, such as firecrackers, kerosene, petrol and gas
Offensive articles that could harm or disturb other passengers
Goods for trade: these must be booked as parcels, not carried as personal luggage
two_wheeler: You can book a scooter or motorcycle as luggage only if you travel on the same train. Otherwise it goes as a parcel.
Empty the petrol tank and pack the vehicle properly.
Carry a photocopy of the registration certificate and a government photo ID, and fill in a forwarding note with the vehicle's make, registration number, weight and value.
Tie a card to the vehicle with the names of the starting and destination stations.
Reach the luggage office at least 30 minutes before departure. The vehicle goes on your train only if there is space, and you collect it with your ticket and luggage ticket.
There is no free allowance for scooters, motorcycles or cycles.
notes: Dogs can travel in an AC First Class or First Class compartment only if your fellow passengers agree and you pay in advance. Otherwise they travel in a dog box in the brake van. Dogs are not allowed in AC sleeper, AC Chair Car, Sleeper or Second Class coaches.
Goods for trade (merchandise) can't travel in the compartment as personal luggage. Book them as parcels.
In the luggage van, a package over 100 kg, or bigger than 1 m x 1 m x 0.7 m, is charged as bulky, at double the normal rate.

If luggage is stolen on the train, tell the TTE, coach attendant, guard or the railway police (GRP) escort. They have FIR forms, so you don't need to break your journey to report it. RPF help posts at big stations can help too.
An oxygen cylinder with its stand is allowed free in all classes for a patient with a medical certificate.
If booked luggage is lost or damaged and you didn't declare its value, the railway pays at most ₹100 per kg.

DD News and other news outlets reported that since 31 July 2026, passengers with confirmed reserved tickets can declare and pay for extra personal luggage online on IRCTC. We couldn't find it on an Indian Railways or IRCTC rules page yet, so the luggage office is still the sure way.
In 2025, news reports said some stations, starting with Prayagraj, plan airport-style luggage weighing. We found no official notice that it has started.

faq.q: How much luggage can I carry free on Indian trains?
faq.a: 70 kg in AC First Class, 50 kg in AC 2-tier and First Class, 40 kg in AC 3-tier, AC Chair Car and Sleeper, and 35 kg in Second Class.

faq.q: Can I take a large suitcase in an AC 3-tier coach?
faq.a: Only up to 55 x 45 x 22.5 cm. Bigger suitcases must be booked in the brake van. In other classes the limit is 100 x 60 x 25 cm.

faq.q: What if my luggage is over the free allowance?
faq.a: Book the extra weight at the luggage office before you travel and pay 1.5 times the luggage rate (minimum ₹30). Unbooked extra luggage found on the train is charged six times the rate (minimum ₹50). In AC 3-tier and AC Chair Car you can't book extra luggage into the coach; it must go in the luggage van.

faq.q: How much luggage can a child carry on a train?
faq.a: Children aged 5 to 11 get half the adult free allowance, up to 50 kg.

faq.q: Can I carry a gas cylinder or firecrackers on a train?
faq.a: No. Explosive, inflammable and dangerous goods, including gas cylinders (even empty ones), are not allowed as luggage.

faq.q: What are the train luggage charges per kg?
faq.a: There is no fixed price per kg. The luggage rate (Scale L) depends on weight and distance. Booked extra luggage costs 1.5 times that rate (minimum ₹30), and unbooked extra luggage found on the train costs six times the rate (minimum ₹50). The station's luggage office gives the exact charge.

faq.q: How do I book luggage on a train?
faq.a: Take your packed and labelled luggage and your journey ticket to the luggage office at the boarding station at least 30 minutes before departure. Pay the charge, keep the luggage ticket, and check that staff have noted it on your journey ticket. News reports say confirmed-ticket passengers can now also pay online on IRCTC, but we couldn't confirm that on an official rules page.

faq.q: How much luggage is allowed in sleeper class per person?
faq.a: 40 kg free. You can book extra and carry up to 80 kg in the coach, paying 1.5 times the luggage rate for the extra. Suitcases up to 100 x 60 x 25 cm can go in a sleeper coach.

faq.q: How much luggage is allowed in Vande Bharat trains?
faq.a: Vande Bharat chair car coaches are AC Chair Car, so you get 40 kg free, and suitcases must be within 55 x 45 x 22.5 cm. The official table doesn't list Executive Chair Car separately, so ask at the luggage office if you need more.

faq.q: Can I take my bike on a train as luggage?
faq.a: Yes, if you travel on the same train. Empty the petrol tank, pack it, and take a copy of the registration certificate and a photo ID to the luggage office at least 30 minutes before departure. There is no free allowance for two-wheelers.

faq.q: What should I do if my luggage is stolen on a train?
faq.a: Tell the TTE, coach attendant, guard or GRP escort on the train. They carry FIR forms, and your complaint is passed to the next police station, so you don't have to get off. RPF help posts at major stations can also help.
